pages.text: Little pig Dingding backed away from the bath, with dirt on their toes and ears. Mom, who worked several paddies on her own, filled the wooden tub.
Dingding hated water on their face and hid behind a post. Still muddy, Dingding wanted to play some more.
Dry mud flaked off. Dingding's arms itched, and Dingding scratched them.
Mr. Ming, who kept ducks in the lowest paddy, waved and called, "Come watch!" Dingding looked down from the doorway.
The ducks sat in the water and flapped their wings. Splash! Splash! Dingding's eyes grew wide.
"Ducks have the most fun washing. Sit in the water, splash, then wipe yourself clean." Mr. Ming sang, "Splash, Splash, Like a Duck!"
Dingding ran to the tub and sat down with a plop. Dingding splashed with both hands while Mom poured water. "Splash, Splash, Like a Duck!"
Dirty water flowed out. Dingding sniffed the cool, watery smell. Bath time was fun!
The next evening, Dingding went to the tub first. "One, sit in the water. Two, splash. Three, wipe and rinse!" The ducks splashed in the paddy below.
Mom wrapped Dingding in a towel and hugged them. "All clean, just like a bathing duck!" Dingding felt fresh, with no more itching, and laughed. "Splash, Splash, Like a Duck!"
